Unemployment is 7.8%, which matches September 2012 (7.8%). Fed funds is about 0.17%, which is consistent with 2012. The 10-year yield at 1.74% fits a late-2012 reading, and CPI at 2.0% YoY fits too. Headline CPI was 2.0% in October 2012, and 1.74% for the 10-year fits October or November. The 3m payroll average of about 146k also fits.

Checking the unemployment path: it fell from 8.2% in June to 7.8% in September, then rose to 7.9% in October and 7.8% in November. The 3m change of -0.4 points implies a reading of 8.2% three months earlier. That points to September (June was 8.2%) or December (September was 7.8%, so no). November's 3m change would be 7.8 against 8.1 in August, which is -0.3. September's would be 7.8 against 8.2 in June, which is -0.4.

CPI: September 2012 was 2.0% and October 2.2%. The 10-year yield was 1.63% at the end of September and 1.65% at the end of October. It was 1.62% at the end of November and 1.76% at the end of December. December 2012 CPI was 1.7% YoY. The 10-year at 1.74% therefore points to a late-December reading, but unemployment in December was 7.8%, and the 3m change from September 7.8% would be 0.0.

The data are as known at the time, so the unemployment series may have been revised. The S&P was -1.8% in the month, which fits November 2012 (+0.6%?), October (-1.9%), or December (+0.9%). October's -1.8% fits best. Gold -2.9% in October is also plausible. The 10-year at 1.74% could be the monthly average rather than month-end. I'll go with October 2012, though that conflicts with 7.9% unemployment for that month. The snapshot says 7.8, which would be the October 2012 reading as first published (7.9%)... I'm uncertain. I'll choose October 2012.
